preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is an integer between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a < b <= n for a, b in edges) and len(edges) == n - 1
preconditions.description: The input graph is a tree with n vertices and exactly n-1 edges, where each edge connects two distinct vertices.

preconditions.expression: len(v) == n and all(abs(x) <= 10**9 for x in v)
preconditions.description: The list v contains exactly n integers, each with absolute value at most 10^9, representing the initial values on the vertices.
The edges form a valid tree structure (connected and acyclic) with vertices numbered from 1 to n.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the minimum number of operations required to make all vertex values zero.

postconditions.expression: let operations = int(stdout); let tree = build_tree(edges, n); let root = 1; let subtree_values = [get_subtree_sum(tree, root, v)]; let target = [0] * n; let possible = all(achievable_with_operations(tree, root, v, operations, target))
postconditions.description: The output integer is the smallest non-negative integer such that there exists a sequence of operations (each operation being an increment/decrement of all vertices in the subtree rooted at vertex 1) that transforms the initial values v into all zeros.

postconditions.expression: let operations = int(stdout); let tree = build_tree(edges, n); let root = 1; let subtree_values = [get_subtree_sum(tree, root, v)]; let target = [0] * n; let minimal = all(min_operations(tree, root, v) == operations)
postconditions.description: The output integer is the minimal number of operations required to achieve the target state where all vertex values are zero, given the constraints of the problem.
